messages.subject: GitHub Landing Page
parts:
It's a somewhat hidden feature of GitHub, but you can have a custom landing page for GitHub.  For example, you can render something nice (like Doxygen) at http://betanalpha.github.com/jamon/ but have you repo still at www.github.com/betanalpha/jamon

If all if this debate about readmes is just about having a nice landing late for users then this might be an option that would allow the repo page to stay clean.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] GitHub Landing Page
parts:
I've never used GitHub before Stan.

I'm thinking of GitHub as being nothing more than our
repository hosting. As such, I want its readme to point
back to our home page and I want the rest of our GitHub
site to be totally minimal.

Maybe this isn't the right way to do it. Maybe we should
just bail on maintaining our own home page and put
all our eggs in the GitHub basket. If we can hack up one
landing page, we can probably add the dozen or so more we
have on our home page.

What I am absolutely opposed to is duplicating all of our
information across several sites. I don't mind a few
high-level overviews, but I don't want the maintenance hassle
of writing the same detailed things that may change in multiple
places.

But please, let's not get too distracted by this issue.

- Bob
